title: Python Data Science Rules
summary: Project rules for Python data science repos: notebooks kept thin, logic in modules, fixed seeds, tidy pandas code and versioned data.
description: Data science repos drift into notebooks nobody can rerun. These rules push reusable logic into a package, keep notebooks for exploration and reporting, and make each result traceable to code, data and a seed.
They also say how to write pandas without hidden mutation, pin environments, and keep large data out of git.
useWhen: A notebook has grown past a few hundred lines
Results change between runs and nobody knows why
Pandas code relies on chained assignment and loops
Data files are being committed to git
body:
# Project rules: Python data science

## Layout
- Put reusable code in a package under `src/` with tests in `tests/`. Notebooks go in `notebooks/`, numbered, and only import from the package. Strip outputs before commit with `nbstripout`.
- Never copy functions between notebooks. Move them into a module the moment a second notebook needs them.

## Reproducibility
- Pin the environment with `pyproject.toml` and a lock file (uv or pip-tools). Record the Python version.
- Set seeds in one place for `random`, NumPy and any model library, and pass a `random_state` to splitters and estimators.
- Keep raw data read-only. Version data and models with DVC or an equivalent, and commit only the pointer files. Never commit credentials or personal data.

## Pandas style
- Prefer vectorized operations and method chaining with `.assign`, `.query` and `.pipe`. Do not loop over rows or modify a frame in place.
- Be explicit: set dtypes on load, name columns in snake_case, use `merge(..., validate=...)` and assert row counts after joins.
- Avoid `SettingWithCopyWarning` by working on copies deliberately.

## Evaluation
- Split before any fitting or scaling to avoid leakage. Report metrics with the split, seed and data version.

## Checks
- Run `ruff check`, `ruff format` and `pytest`. Tests cover transform functions with small hand-made frames.

example.prompt: Clean the sales export and add a monthly revenue feature
example.result: The agent writes a typed function in src/sales/features.py, loads with explicit dtypes, validates the join, adds a pytest case with a three-row frame and calls it from a numbered notebook.

faq.question: Should notebooks be banned?
faq.answer: No. They are good for exploring and presenting. The rule is only that real logic does not live in them.

faq.question: Which data versioning tool is required?
faq.answer: None in particular. DVC is named as an example; any tool that keeps data out of git and records versions works.

access: Instructions only; it does not read or run anything by itself
